newsitem.title: CONGO: Fresh lull in Brazzaville after heavy shelling.
newsitem.headline: Fresh lull in Brazzaville after heavy shelling.

text.p: Congo's divided capital Brazzaville enjoyed a fresh bout of relative calm on Thursday, the morning after an evening of heavy shelling around the international airport and in the city centre.
Witnesses said some isolated shooting continued, but that it was nothing compared to what was heard on Wednesday after nightfall.

Diplomats said efforts -- both domestic and international -- to find a solution to the month-long showdown between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor, former military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso, continued.
Witnesses said Wednesday night's city centre shelling was near Tour Nabemba, close to the frontline separating the area controlled by Lissouba from the districts in the hands of Sassou.

The fighting, which began on June 5 after Lissouba tried to disarm Sassou's private militia, has killed hundreds of people and sent tens of thousands fleeing the city or to the relatively calmer southern suburbs.
